outcome: Diagnostic efficacy of plasma D-dimer for excluding VTE
cohort: 514 pregnant and puerperal women (cohort 1) and 29 puerperal women who developed VTE 24-48 hours after cesarean section (cohort 2)
finding: Plasma D-dimer levels were higher in pregnant and puerperal women compared to non-pregnant women, and D-dimer had good value in diagnosing and excluding VTE during early puerperium after cesarean section.
mod_finding: The plasma D-dimer levels of the cesarean section subgroup at 24-48 h postpartum were significantly higher than those of the vaginal delivery subgroup (P < 0.05).
